title: Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus
source: Capitoline Museums first-floor visitor plan aligned to retained Protomaps building geometry.
axis: +X follows the foundation northwest toward the Esedra. +Z faces east-northeast into the photographed gallery. +Y is vertical.

nativeAxes.x: northwest along the exposed eastern foundation

identityStatus: The museum first-floor visitor drawing places rooms 17 and 18 beside the curved Esedra. Four mapped courtyard corners align the drawing, and the curved hall independently checks the registration. The visible eastern foundation trace determines the length and axis. The geotagged 2024 photograph falls on the modeled face side.

reconstruction.scope: Exposed eastern tufa foundation and stepped podium masonry of the Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus in the Capitoline Museums.

reconstruction.heightBasis: The approximately 20 m exposed run derives from the registered public plan. Block dimensions, the stepped crest and the upper preserved courses are interpreted from the museum photographs.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: The retained museum datum establishes a common vertical reference for the authored visitor room and tufa foundation. The display floor is reconstructed from public views and the standard terrain. Relative grades share the present-day museum heightfield.
